demarcationCarriedVerbatim.permittedFunctions: The proposed common control plane may only: discover authenticated manifest capabilities; start/stop/supervise a component; negotiate an opaque named role subprotocol and version; carry cancellation/health/resource/fault control; and broker separately authorized host effects.
demarcationCarriedVerbatim.mustNotList: It must not wrap, translate, normalize, reorder, reinterpret, merge, or assign new fates to semantic frames of an existing provider protocol.
demarcationCarriedVerbatim.racesAndJoins: Host control events and opaque provider data may race, but precedence remains host-owned and deterministic. The host defines joins for cancellation versus result, control fault versus provider fault, EOF/process death, duplicate or late frames, and teardown. Hostile dual-channel conformance exercises every ordering while comparing provider semantic frames byte-for-byte: the control plane may decide supervision/fate only under the owning contract and cannot translate provider meaning to resolve a race.
demarcationCarriedVerbatim.closingRule: Any semantic frame/fate or lifetime change to either protocol needs an explicit successor from the owning V1 surface. The common control protocol cannot make the change by negotiation.

measuredProviderTransportBindings.consequence: Because the applied provider contracts own stdin/stdout in full - protocol-only from process start through EOF - the control plane CANNOT lawfully share, multiplex, or wrap those streams. framing.frame: A control frame is: a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length N, followed by exactly N bytes of frame body. N counts the body only, not the prefix.

bounds.preHandshake: Until helloAck is accepted, N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0 is refusal family RF-2, detected from the prefix alone; the receiver must refuse without buffering the body. Rationale: bound memory before any trust or negotiation exists.
bounds.postHandshake: After helloAck, the operative bound is the negotiated maxControlFrameBytes (handshake field): the component may accept less than the host offer but never less than 65536; the ceiling either side may offer or accept is 16777216. A frame exceeding the negotiated bound is RF-2.
bounds.constantsStatus: 65536 and 16777216 are DESIGN-CHOSEN protocol constants proposed by this candidate, reviewable like any other clause; they are not measurements and carry no workload claim. Control frames carry no bulk payload by design - bulk rides the data plane or a brokered host effect - so the ceiling is a hostile-input bound, not a throughput promise. Operational timeout/deadline VALUES are deliberately not bound here (see joinPrecedenceTable.deadlineDiscipline) because a numeric threshold without a named runner/workload measures nothing (the D-006 lesson recorded in D-007's alternatives).

framing.sequencing: Every frame body carries a seq member: per-direction, starting at 1, incrementing by exactly 1. A gap, repeat, or decrease is refusal family RF-7. seq is bounded by the integer rule at controlFrameEncoding (uint53); a frame whose seq exceeds that bound is RF-7. There is no overflow or wraparound handling, and the ceiling carries no workload rationale: this contract binds no per-channel frame-count bound, so every seq below the ceiling is individually lawful, and the uint53 limit stands as a bare protocol constant whose violation is typed - nothing more is claimed for it.
framing.channelState: The control channel is a closed state machine: AWAIT-HELLO -> AWAIT-HELLO-ACK -> AWAIT-SELECT -> AWAIT-SELECT-ACK -> STEADY -> TEARDOWN -> CLOSED, plus FAULTED reachable from every state. On the first violation the receiver emits its typed refusal (when the channel is still writable), stops reading the violating direction, records the event in the merged order (joinPrecedenceTable), and proceeds by the teardown ladder. There is no resynchronization, no skip-and-continue, and no best-effort parse in any state.

controlFrameEncoding.encoding: A frame body is one UTF-8 JSON text (RFC 8259) whose top level is a single object. Parse-level strictness, applied by every receiver: duplicate member names anywhere reject the frame (RF-2); a non-object top level rejects; unknown members at any level reject (RF-2) - there is no ignorable-extension mechanism in major 1, so nothing can be smuggled through tolerated members; numbers are permitted only as integers with exact magnitude at most 9007199254740991 (uint53, non-negative), so every conforming parser holds every permitted value exactly and no float admission hazard exists; any other numeric form is RF-2.
controlFrameEncoding.nonCanonicalByConstruction: The encoding is deliberately NON-CANONICAL: any RFC 8259-valid serialization of the same message value is equally lawful on the wire. Member order, whitespace, and string-escape choices are meaningless. It is a conformance obligation (class CC-11) that two byte-different serializations of the same message value produce identical protocol behavior. Consequently NOTHING may derive identity, signature, digest, equality-of-record, or any evidence commitment from control-frame BYTES; digests carried INSIDE control frames (for example admittedManifestDigest) are data computed by their owning surfaces over their own bytes, never by this protocol over its frames.

encodingProfileDecision.decision: Specify a non-canonical length-prefixed encoding that never requires byte-determinism; do NOT ride the canonical-profile surface and do NOT invent a canonicalization.
encodingProfileDecision.why: The only artifact that could supply a canonical JSON profile (canonical-json-profile.v1.json, measured at digest above) is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with UR-1..UR-5 open, and inventing key-ordering/escaping/numeric normalization here is exactly the discipline violation the corpus forbids. The control plane has no need for byte-determinism: control frames are parsed, validated, acted on, and discarded; no identity is minted from them. Choosing non-canonical encoding plus a hard no-identity-from-control-bytes rule removes the ride entirely - one fewer open surface this contract waits on - and makes the temptation to hash control frames a specified violation rather than an ambiguity. If a successor ever needs identity over control bytes, that successor must ride the canonical-profile closure explicitly (identityDependencies ID-DEP-7).
encodingProfileDecision.alternativeRejected: Canonical-CBOR control frames (mirroring the provider planes) were rejected: byte-determinism would still be unnecessary, the RFC 8949 deterministic-encoding discipline would import exactly the class of canonicalization obligations this contract avoids, and visual symmetry with the provider planes would invite the false reading that control and provider frames share a wire universe. They must not: provider frames are sealed opaque bytes here.

controlFrameEncoding.messageEnvelope: Every frame body object has exactly these members: type (string, closed vocabulary at capabilityEnvelope.messageVocabulary), seq (integer, per framing.sequencing), controlMajor (integer; fixed at the negotiated major after hello), body (object; per-type schema). The frozen refusal core: the framing rule, the four-member envelope, and the refusal message-type schema are FROZEN across all future control-protocol majors, so a future-major hello can always be refused typed by an older implementation without parsing anything beyond the envelope. This freeze is the mechanism behind the DR-111 row's future-major-refusal cell.

handshake.ownVersionSurface: The control protocol versions ITSELF: proposed controlProtocolMajor = 1 for this candidate. It is its own DR-111 compatibility-matrix row (file 04 line 175 names 'common control protocol' as a separate surface), NEVER a shared version with either provider protocol, the distribution core, or any component release. TypeScript provider major 1 and Rust provider major 2 are versions of THEIR surfaces; the numeric coincidence with controlMajor 1 carries no meaning and no coupling (file 02: 'There is no required same-version coupling').

sequence.body: controlMajor; expectedStableId (the admitted component's author-declared immutable UUID, per the CANDIDATE manifest schema's stableId field and D-012 clause 1); admittedManifestDigest (lowercase-hex sha256 of the admitted manifest bytes as recorded by the admission surface - carried as DATA, computed by admission, never recomputed by this protocol); platform { os, arch } (the platform alternative the host resolved); maxControlFrameBytesOffer; subprotocolOffers: array of { role, roleSubprotocol, subprotocolVersion } tuples.

controlMajor (must equal the hello's; a helloAck proposing a different controlMajor is RF-8); stableId and admittedManifestDigest echoed VERBATIM; maxControlFrameBytes (at most the offer, at least 65536); subprotocolConfirms: a subset of subprotocolOffers, compared tuple-by-tuple under the opacity rules at opaqueSubprotocolNegotiation. Any echo mismatch is RF-3. A component that does not support the offered controlMajor responds instead with refusal { family: RF-1, supportedControlMajors: [...] } and the channel proceeds to teardown; it must not attempt to parse the hello body beyond the frozen envelope.

Exactly one tuple from subprotocolConfirms. If subprotocolConfirms is empty or the host declines every confirmed tuple, the host sends shutdown instead and the session was a control-only session (lawful: supervision without a data plane).

The selected tuple echoed verbatim. After selectAck, and only after it, the data plane (fd0/fd1) is live for the selected subprotocol under its OWNING contract - including that contract's own in-band handshake (for example the TypeScript provider's Hello frame), which is a semantic frame of the provider protocol: sealed, opaque, byte-preserved, and invisible to the control plane.

handshake.identityBindingHonesty: The stableId/digest echo is a CHANNEL-BINDING AGREEMENT CHECK, not authentication and not proof of anything: a process that can echo is not thereby the admitted bytes. What makes the child the admitted component is exact-byte admission plus verification-bound-to-spawn (file 04; DR-G07) and the signing/trust chain (DR-112, OPEN - identityDependencies ID-DEP-4). The bound is the claim: the handshake detects wiring mistakes (wrong child on the pipe, stale generation) deterministically; it defends against nothing an adversary inside the process boundary could do.
downgradeAndRefusalRules: Exactly one hello per channel lifetime. A second hello in any state is RF-8.

There is no version renegotiation, no downgrade path, and no minor-version concept on the wire: majors are the only compatibility unit, and windows across majors live in the DR-111 matrix row, not in the channel.
A future-major hello is refused TYPED via the frozen refusal core - never best-effort parsed, never partially applied.
A hello whose expectedStableId or admittedManifestDigest does not match the receiving component's admitted identity data is RF-3 - refused, never 'corrected' by either side.
Refusals are loud and terminal for the channel: every refusal family leads through the teardown ladder; no refusal is retryable within the same channel.

opaqueSubprotocolNegotiation.principle: The control plane may SELECT and CONFIRM a (role, roleSubprotocol, subprotocolVersion) tuple; it may never inspect, interpret, translate, or version-bridge the subprotocol's content. TypeScript provider major 1 and Rust provider major 2 pass through as sealed byte streams. The closing rule, verbatim (file 02): 'Any semantic frame/fate or lifetime change to either protocol needs an explicit successor from the owning V1 surface. The common control protocol cannot make the change by negotiation.'

tokenOpacity.comparison: role and roleSubprotocol are OPAQUE tokens: compared by exact Unicode code-point sequence equality of the declared and offered strings - no case folding, no Unicode normalization (no NFC/NFKC), no trimming, no aliasing, no substring or pattern matching. subprotocolVersion is an opaque integer compared by exact equality - the control plane attaches no ordering semantics to it (it does not know that 2 is 'newer' than 1, and MUST not act as if it does; version windows are the DR-111 matrix row of the OWNING subprotocol surface).
tokenOpacity.custody: Per D-012, a subprotocol name means nothing as a raw string: it resolves THROUGH the admitted component's stableId custody - the offer set is constructed from the capabilities[] declarations of the manifest admitted for THIS (stableId, provenance) pair, and a token's meaning is 'the thing that manifest declared', never 'any component anywhere that uses this string'. Two components declaring the same roleSubprotocol string share nothing by that fact alone.

opaqueSubprotocolNegotiation.offerConstruction: subprotocolOffers is derived host-side, metadata-only, from: (a) the authenticated admitted manifest's capabilities[] declarations (CANDIDATE manifest schema, cited at digest - identityDependencies ID-DEP-1), intersected with (b) the operation's pinned generation/lock selection where one exists (file 04: locks select 'subprotocol/state formats'; each operation pins its generation for its lifetime - identityDependencies ID-DEP-6). The component is never asked to self-describe at runtime: D-012's metadata-only admission rule extends here - there is no discovery query message, and a component volunteering capability data outside helloAck's confirm-subset is RF-4.
whatNegotiationCanNever: Offer a tuple absent from the admitted manifest's declarations (host-side violation; conformance class CC-7 proves the component side refuses spoofed offers too).
Confirm a tuple absent from the hello's offer set (RF-4).
Map, alias, or 'upgrade' one subprotocol or version to another - no tuple in, tuple out transformation exists in the vocabulary.

Carry any member whose value is drawn from a provider protocol's frame vocabulary: fates, frame types, verdicts, Coverage states, and D9 codes are structurally absent from every control message schema (fate-assignment smuggling is CC-8).
Change what the selected subprotocol means: selection binds WHICH sealed contract runs on the data plane, nothing about its content.
opaqueSubprotocolNegotiation.lifetimeNeutrality: Negotiation and the control channel add no lifetime rights: one child per (ExecutionId, SnapshotId, TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey) and no reuse for TypeScript major 1, one supervised sidecar per semantic universe and no reuse for Rust major 2, and R-1 lifetime-neutrality all stand exactly as the owning contracts state them (file 02). The control plane cannot keep a child alive for a later request, pool children, or re-negotiate a live channel to a second tuple: one select per channel, one channel per child, ever.

capabilityEnvelope.exhaustiveness: The five permitted functions (demarcationCarriedVerbatim.permittedFunctions) are the EXHAUSTIVE capability envelope of the control plane. The closed sixteen-message vocabulary divides mechanically in two: every message except refusal belongs to EXACTLY ONE function family below, and refusal is the envelope's single cross-cutting enforcement message, excluded BY NAME from the family rule and defined at crossCuttingEnforcement. Checkable form, true on this artifact's own bytes: (a) the union of functions[].messages equals messageVocabulary minus ['refusal']; (b) the functions[].messages lists are pairwise disjoint; (c) 'refusal' appears in messageVocabulary, is named at crossCuttingEnforcement.message, and appears in no functions[].messages list. Anything else - any unknown type, any known type outside its lawful state, any request for a sixth function - is refused via that same refusal message, typed by family at refusalFamilies. The vocabulary is closed: a control-protocol major defines its complete message list, and extension happens only by a new major through the DR-111 row.

crossCuttingEnforcement.definition: refusal is the typed negative outcome of the WHOLE envelope, not a sixth capability: either side, in any channel state, emits it on detecting a violation (component -> host on fd4, host -> component on fd3), carrying its family (RF-1..RF-8) and that family's bounded detail members under the frozen refusal core (controlFrameEncoding.messageEnvelope). It is enforcement-only - never solicited, never a request, never carrying capability data - and it is terminal for the channel per refusalFamilies.discipline: every refusal leads through the teardown ladder.
crossCuttingEnforcement.whyOutsideTheFamilyRule: Refusal cannot belong to one family because enforcement precedes classification: an RF-2 frame violation is detected before any parse assigns the frame a family, and refusing an unknown type refuses a message no family contains. Placing refusal inside a single family would falsify that family's boundary the first time another family's exchange was refused; declaring it cross-cutting BY NAME keeps the family rule exhaustive over the other fifteen messages and keeps the whole claim mechanically checkable (exhaustiveness clauses a-c). It smuggles no sixth function: it requests nothing, carries no capability, and can only end a channel, never extend one.

functions.onTheWire: Deliberately NOT a wire function: discovery is host-side reading of authenticated admitted metadata (file 02: help/completion/inventory 'read authenticated metadata only'; D-012: no execution during discovery). The channel carries discovery's RESULT - the offer set in hello - and nothing else. There is no describe/list/query message; a runtime self-description request in either direction is RF-4.

Spawn and reap are host process actions bracketing the channel; on the wire this family is the session frame: hello/helloAck open supervision, shutdown/shutdownAck and the teardown ladder close it, ping/pong provides liveness.

functions.function: negotiate an opaque named role subprotocol and version
functions.onTheWire: select/selectAck over the hello/helloAck offer/confirm sets, per opaqueSubprotocolNegotiation.

cancel (host -> component): SUPERVISION-SCOPED - it announces that teardown is beginning and gives the component its bounded chance to stop cleanly; it is not an in-band data-plane message and never becomes one (see tensionsObserved T-1: the TypeScript provider's own Cancel frame belongs to the provider protocol's host-side participant, not to this plane). health (host -> component) / healthReport (component -> host): liveness and declared-load reporting. resourceReport (component -> host): bounded structural report (integers and strings under the encoding rules). fault (component -> host): the component reports an internal failure with a bounded detail string; what that failure MEANS - fate, D9, exit - is decided under the owning contracts and DR-007's successor (identityDependencies ID-DEP-2), never by this message.

effectRequest (component -> host) names an effect class token and an authorizationRef; effectResult (host -> component) returns a typed outcome. AUTHORIZATION IS NOT GRANTED BY THIS PROTOCOL: the channel is a courier; whether the effect is permitted is decided by the host's permission/policy surfaces against the admitted manifest's declarations (DR-105 scope per D-002; broker semantics under DR-125's contract - identityDependencies ID-DEP-5). An effectRequest with no valid separate authorization is refused typed (RF-6), and the refusal is an outcome, not a nudge to retry.

refusalFamilies.discipline: Typed, loud, terminal-for-the-channel, and surface-local: these family identifiers name control-plane refusal classes ONLY. They are not D9 codes, not exit codes, not fates, and never map to any of those by this artifact - the mapping enters solely through DR-007's successor chain (identityDependencies ID-DEP-2). This mirrors the CANDIDATE manifest schema's refusal-code discipline.

families.name: control-version-unsupported
families.covers: hello with a controlMajor the receiver does not implement; refused via the frozen refusal core with supportedControlMajors listed; never best-effort parsed.

families.name: frame-violation
families.covers: length prefix of 0, oversize against the operative bound, truncated body, invalid UTF-8, non-object top level, duplicate members, unknown members, non-integer or out-of-range numerics.

families.name: identity-binding-mismatch
families.covers: stableId or admittedManifestDigest echo mismatch in either direction.

families.name: undeclared-capability
families.covers: confirming a tuple not offered; offering/confirming a tuple absent from admitted manifest declarations; any runtime self-description or discovery query; capability data volunteered outside helloAck.

families.name: semantic-content-request
families.covers: any control message asking the control plane to inspect, transform, reframe, re-fate, or adjudicate provider-protocol content - the wire form of the must-not list; includes fate-assignment smuggling (CC-8).

families.name: unauthorized-host-effect
families.covers: effectRequest without valid separate authorization, for an unknown effect class, or exceeding the authorization's scope.

families.name: protocol-state-violation
families.covers: seq gap/repeat/decrease; a known type in an unlawful state; frames after shutdownAck; data-plane bytes before selectAck (CH-DATA-EARLY); duplicate or late control frames per join J-4.

families.name: handshake-replay-or-downgrade
families.covers: a second hello in any state; a helloAck proposing a controlMajor different from the hello's (in-channel version movement - the downgrade/renegotiation attempt in wire form; detected host-side, since helloAck flows component -> host); any attempt to re-enter negotiation or re-select on a live channel.

nonTranslationObligation.octetIdentityProperty: The data-plane pass-through is an OCTET-SEQUENCE IDENTITY: the octet sequence the component emits on fd1 is exactly the octet sequence the owning provider contract's host-side participant receives - equal length, equal bytes, equal order - and symmetrically for fd0 in the host-to-component direction. No insertion, deletion, substitution, reordering, or duplication of octets. The identity is stated over the octet sequence ONLY, because that is all this transport can carry: fd0/fd1 are POSIX pipes, byte streams that preserve no write boundaries, so no obligation over carrier write boundaries is enforceable here and none is stated. Both existing majors frame IN-BAND (length-delimited canonical CBOR, self-delimiting), so the enforceable frame-level obligation lives at the framing layer: after boundary recovery under the owning contract's own framing, the recovered frames must be byte-for-byte equal in equal order (judged exactly so by CC-1, CC-2, CC-9). A future subprotocol whose framing depends on carrier write boundaries cannot lawfully be carried on this transport at all: admitting one requires an explicit successor that changes the transport, and no clause of this contract may be read as promising boundary preservation the pipe does not provide.
nonTranslationObligation.structuralEnforcement: This candidate's descriptor layout makes the property structural: fd0/fd1 connect the component to the host's provider-side participant directly, and the control plane holds no read or write interest in them (transportAndFraming.descriptorLayout). The control plane cannot mistranslate bytes it never holds. Hostile conformance still PROVES the property end-to-end (classes CC-1, CC-2, CC-9) rather than trusting the layout: the bound is the claim, and the claim is proven byte-for-byte, not assumed from plumbing.
nonTranslationObligation.mustNotListCarriedVerbatim: It must not wrap, translate, normalize, reorder, reinterpret, merge, or assign new fates to semantic frames of an existing provider protocol.
nonTranslationObligation.noSuppressionRule: Suppressing provider octets IS assigning a fate: after cancel is issued and until data-plane EOF, arriving provider octets are still delivered unmodified in order to the owning contract's participant, which alone decides what late data means under its own rules. The control plane never closes, drains-to-null, or edits the data plane mid-stream; it only observes EOF and process death as events in the merged order.
nonTranslationObligation.closingRuleCarriedVerbatim: Any semantic frame/fate or lifetime change to either protocol needs an explicit successor from the owning V1 surface. The common control protocol cannot make the change by negotiation.

joinPrecedenceTable.mechanism: The host maintains ONE host-owned merged event order per supervised child: an append-only total order over control-plane events (frame accepted, refusal, cancel issued, shutdown issued, deadline expiry) and data-plane boundary events (first byte, EOF, process death, and the owning participant's fault report per J-2 - boundary events and boundary reports only, never content). Each event is appended at host observation with its channel and kind. Determinism claim, bounded: given the same observed event sequence per channel and the tie rules below, the merged order is a pure function of those observations - the joins bind ORDERING. What any ordering MEANS - fates, D9, exits, Coverage - is decided under the OWNING contract and is DR-007-open; no code value appears in this table (identityDependencies ID-DEP-2).

joins.rule: cancel-issued is appended when the host writes the cancel frame; a provider result is represented by its final-octet arrival within the data-plane stream (content invisible; the owning participant reports 'stream position P complete' as a boundary fact). If the final octet was read before cancel was written, the result precedes the cancel in the merged order; otherwise cancel precedes. Same-observation-instant tie: the data-plane event is appended first (a byte that has arrived is history; the host's own control action never retroactively outranks received bytes). The owning contract then decides what a result-after-cancel or cancel-after-result IS.

A control-plane fault (any RF family) and a provider-plane fault (as defined by the owning contract, surfaced to the host as a boundary event, e.g. EOF-mid-stream or the owning participant's fault report) are both appended at observation. The earlier event drives the supervision transition (which ladder step starts); the later one is still appended and delivered - never coalesced, never dropped. Same-instant tie: the control-plane fault is appended first, because supervision is this plane's own authority while the provider fault's meaning belongs to the owning contract; ordering first does not let the control fault redefine the provider fault.

EOF is per-channel (fd1, fd4 observed separately); process death (reaped exit status) is a distinct event. All channels are drained to EOF - every octet read and delivered - before the death event is appended, under a bounded host drain deadline whose expiry is itself a typed appended event (drain-deadline-expired) that precedes the death event when it fires. Death is therefore always the LAST event of a child's merged order, and no octet that arrived before death can be lost behind it.

Duplicate/out-of-order CONTROL frames: seq discipline makes them RF-7 at the receiver - typed, appended, never silently dropped, never reordered-to-fit. Late CONTROL frames after shutdownAck: RF-7, appended after the shutdown event they violate. Late PROVIDER data after cancel or teardown initiation: delivered unmodified per the no-suppression rule, appended in arrival order; the owning contract alone assigns its meaning. The control plane has no concept of a provider duplicate: recognizing one would require reading content.

The teardown ladder is deterministic and one-way: T-1 shutdown frame (or cancel, when teardown begins as cancellation) -> T-2 bounded wait for shutdownAck and voluntary exit -> T-3 data-plane and control-plane EOF observation with J-3 draining -> T-4 kill of the full process tree -> T-5 reap and final death event. Each transition is an appended event; expiry of each bounded wait is an appended typed event; the ladder never skips backward and teardown never truncates or rewrites the merged order retroactively.

joinPrecedenceTable.deadlineDiscipline: Every 'bounded wait' above MUST exist, MUST be finite, and its expiry MUST be a typed appended event - that is bound HERE. The numeric values are host operational configuration bound at blueprint/qualification, NOT here: a duration constant without a named runner and workload would be a threshold that measures nothing, and the containment harness (DR-G21) is where expiry behavior gets its goldens (identityDependencies ID-DEP-3).

hostileDualChannelConformance.discipline: Fixture CLASSES with exact-byte intent - what is injected, what must hold, and how equality is judged - not implementations. Every class that touches the data plane judges provider semantic frames BYTE-FOR-BYTE against the injected reference stream: equality means equal octet sequences per frame after boundary recovery under the owning contract's own framing, and equal frame order. The harness that executes these classes is DR-G21/blueprint work (identityDependencies ID-DEP-3); acceptance for DR-102 is 'contract proving no TS/Rust frame translation plus hostile conformance', and these classes are the hostile half's specification.

classes.name: race-ordering matrix
classes.intent: Every pairwise and every reachable total ordering of {cancel-issued, provider-final-octet, control-fault, provider-fault-report, provider-EOF, process-death, teardown-initiated} is exercised with scripted channel actors. provider-fault-report is the owning participant's fault report surfaced to the host as a boundary event - J-2's second provider-fault constituent - injected by the scripted owning-side actor as a boundary report whose content the control plane never reads. For each ordering the merged event order must match the J-1..J-5 rules exactly, including every J-2 variant in which the provider fault is the fault report rather than an EOF and the same-observation-instant tie J-2 resolves control-fault-first, and the provider byte stream delivered to the owning participant must equal the injected stream byte-for-byte in every ordering - a race may change WHAT the order says, never one provider octet.

classes.name: mid-frame interleave
classes.intent: Control frames (ping, cancel, health, shutdown) delivered while a provider frame is partially transmitted on the data plane - including split at every byte offset of the provider frame's length prefix and at chunk sizes of 1 byte. The provider frame must arrive byte-identical with boundaries intact; the control frames must be processed normally; no cross-channel buffering artifact may reorder either plane's own events.

classes.name: duplicate/late/reordered control frames
classes.intent: seq repeats, gaps, decreases; frames replayed after their state window; frames after shutdownAck. Each is RF-7 typed at first violation; the provider stream in flight remains byte-identical; the violation event lands in the merged order exactly once.

classes.name: EOF at every state
classes.intent: fd3/fd4/fd1 EOF and process death injected at EVERY channel state (AWAIT-HELLO through TEARDOWN) and at every handshake step boundary. Every case yields the typed J-3 ordering (drain, then death last); no state yields a partial-parse acceptance, a hang without a bounded-wait expiry event, or a fabricated success.

classes.name: oversized and malformed framing
classes.intent: Length prefix 0; prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound (pre- and post-handshake bounds separately); truncated bodies; invalid UTF-8; duplicate members; unknown members; floats, negative and over-uint53 integers. Each is RF-2 typed; the fixture's pass property includes the observable memory bound - the receiver refuses oversize from the prefix alone without buffering the body.

classes.name: handshake downgrade and replay
classes.intent: Future-major hello (typed RF-1 via the frozen core, with the body deliberately laden with hostile content that must never be parsed); second hello in every state (RF-8); helloAck proposing a different controlMajor than offered (RF-8); re-select attempts after selectAck (RF-8). No downgrade path exists to find: pass means every attempt ends in the typed refusal plus teardown ladder, never a lower-version session.

classes.name: subprotocol-name spoofing versus manifest declarations
classes.intent: Offers and confirms carrying tokens outside the admitted manifest's capabilities[] declarations: case variants, NFC/NFKC-equal-but-code-point-different variants, homoglyphs, trailing/leading whitespace, zero-width insertions, same string declared by a DIFFERENT stableId's manifest, and subprotocolVersion off-by-one. Every one is RF-4 under exact code-point/integer equality against THIS component's admitted declarations; nothing normalizes, nothing fuzzy-matches, no cross-component custody leak.

classes.name: fate-assignment smuggling
classes.intent: Control frames attempting to carry provider meaning: members named or valued after fates/verdicts/D9/Coverage/frame types, an effectRequest asking the host to 'retry the analysis', a fault report embedding a claimed provider verdict, a cancel scoped to 'discard the last result'. Each is RF-5 (or RF-2 where the member is unknown) and the fixture proves the provider stream and the owning contract's view of it are bit-identical to the no-smuggling run - the attempt must be inert, not merely refused.

classes.name: pass-through byte identity under stress
classes.intent: Chunk-boundary fuzzing on the data plane: 1-byte writes, maximum-size writes, pathological flush patterns, interleavings with heavy control traffic, cancellation mid-stream. Reassembled provider octet sequence identical to injected in every run; frame-boundary recovery under the owning contract's own in-band framing yields byte-for-byte equal frames in equal order. No fixture declares a subprotocol sensitive to carrier write boundaries: the pipe transport preserves none (nonTranslationObligation.octetIdentityProperty), so such a subprotocol is untransportable here by contract - a fixture-design error, not a conformance dimension.

classes.name: identity-binding mismatch
classes.intent: helloAck echoing a wrong stableId, wrong digest, digest in wrong case or truncated; hello sent with a stableId/digest for a different admitted component. Each is RF-3 typed from either side; no session reaches select; the mismatch event is recorded once in the merged order.

classes.name: non-canonical encoding indifference
classes.intent: Semantically identical control messages serialized with different member orders, whitespace, and string escapes drive byte-different frames through identical protocol behavior: identical state transitions, identical merged event order, identical responses. The bound is the claim: these fixtures show serialization indifference on the exercised vectors and nothing more - a finite fixture set cannot prove the universal negative that no receiver anywhere compares control frames by bytes. That universal rule remains a specified obligation at controlFrameEncoding.nonCanonicalByConstruction; CC-11 is its testable witness, and any receiver whose behavior differs across these byte-different serializations fails.

compatibilityMatrixRow.assertion: The common control protocol is its OWN row in DR-111's per-surface matrices (file 04 line 175, measured). This candidate proposes that row's content skeleton: current writer = controlProtocolMajor 1; supported readers = major 1 exactly (no cross-major window exists yet, and none can exist before a second major does); future-major refusal = typed via the frozen refusal core (RF-1), never best-effort parse; downgrade/no-return = no in-channel downgrade path exists (RF-8), so version movement happens only by host and component release selection through signed metadata; migrations/bridges = NONE for provider content ever (the closing rule; a 'bridge' cell in this row can only ever describe CONTROL-frame accommodation, and any reading of DR-111 bridge vocabulary as authorizing provider-frame bridging is foreclosed by the demarcation - see tensionsObserved T-3). Window SEMANTICS and the matrix's test-evidence cells are DR-111's to define: identityDependencies ID-DEP-8.

identityDependencies.pattern: Named per the D-002 symmetry-clause pattern (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, Identity dependencies section, measured at digest): each dependency names the open surface it rides, presumes nothing settled, and if the named surface closes by scoped disposition rather than a binding artifact, the dependent feature here ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits, by that disposition's terms; none of it survives on prose. Nothing this contract rides is ridden silently.

dependencies.feature: Negotiation offer/confirm sets; hello's expectedStableId and admittedManifestDigest fields
dependencies.ridesOn: DR-103 (OPEN) via component-manifest-schemas.v1.json (CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, sha256 2733d766dbf94ea98e97286bcd586d782175c69d19e54a3858b26d3787ac8543, under independent review at authoring) - the capabilities[] declaration shape and the stableId identity model (itself D-012's decided policy).
dependencies.consequence: If DR-103 closes with a different declaration shape, the offer-set construction and handshake identity fields follow the applied schema by successor; this contract's negotiation section re-binds to the applied field names and shapes, and no negotiation ships against the candidate schema's shape on prose.

dependencies.feature: Meaning of refusal families, fault reports, and every join outcome - fates, D9 codes, exit codes
dependencies.ridesOn: DR-007's successor chain (HARD-BLOCKED at measurement: 'V2 cannot define replay/purge/degradation typed result or exit').
dependencies.consequence: RF-1..RF-8 and the J-1..J-5 orderings bind ORDERING and refusal-class identity only, as surface-local names. Their integration into D9/exits enters solely by the owning successor; if that closure is a scoped disposition, the affected mappings follow its terms and nothing here pre-empts them.

dependencies.feature: Execution of the hostile dual-channel conformance classes; deadline-expiry goldens; crash/reap containment evidence
dependencies.ridesOn: DR-G21 (component-failure-containment gate) and the blueprint-phase harness work.
dependencies.consequence: CC-1..CC-11 are specifications of intent and pass properties; DR-102's acceptance-evidence cell is discharged only when a harness executes them. If DR-G21 lands scoped, the conformance surface rescopes with it.

dependencies.ridesOn: DR-112 (OPEN: signing/trust/revocation state machine) and DR-G07 with file 04's verification-bound-to-spawn requirement (DR-107 lifecycle chain).
dependencies.consequence: The echo check stays an agreement check (handshake.identityBindingHonesty). Any claim that a control session is a TRUSTED session enters only when those surfaces close; this contract never states it.

dependencies.feature: Broker semantics behind F-5; envelope/diagnostic taxonomy that healthReport/resourceReport/fault details feed into; SDK surface that components program against
dependencies.ridesOn: DR-125 (OPEN: common component SDK/control contract owns cross-cutting product behavior) and DR-105's slice-scoped permissions (D-002).
dependencies.consequence: This contract binds the COURIER: message existence, framing, direction, refusal families. Effect-class vocabularies, authorization shapes, and diagnostic taxonomies are DR-125-owned; exact SDK APIs stay out of scope entirely (whatThisDoesNotDo item 2). If DR-125 closes scoped, F-4/F-5 body vocabularies follow its terms.

dependencies.ridesOn: DR-107 (lifecycle/generation mechanism) and file 04's lock model.

dependencies.feature: Canonical encoding profile - DELIBERATELY NOT RIDDEN
dependencies.ridesOn: Nothing. canonical-json-profile.v1.json was measured (CANDIDATE, UR-1..UR-5 open) precisely to record that this contract does not ride it: control frames are non-canonical by construction and no identity is derived from control bytes.
dependencies.consequence: Symmetry clause, stated forward at the prohibition's full width (controlFrameEncoding.nonCanonicalByConstruction): if any successor ever derives identity, signature, digest, equality-of-record, or any evidence commitment from control-frame BYTES - including byte-comparing logged control frames for audit-log replay equality, or indexing/keying any record by a digest of frame bytes - THAT successor acquires the canonical-profile ride explicitly and must wait on or cite its closure; it cannot inherit lawfulness from this artifact's non-canonical stance.

dependencies.feature: Compatibility-window semantics, reader/writer matrix cells, and cross-version test evidence for the control protocol's own row
dependencies.consequence: compatibilityMatrixRow proposes skeleton content; the matrix's semantics and evidence discipline are DR-111's. If DR-111 closes scoped, this row's cells follow that disposition.

whatThisDoesNotDo: 1. Change, extend, reinterpret, or version-bridge either provider protocol: TypeScript major 1 (applied delivery.v4 over delivery.v2) and Rust major 2 (the four-artifact merge) pass through as sealed byte streams; the closing rule is carried verbatim twice above.
2. Design SDK APIs, frameworks, or component-facing programming surfaces (DR-125 territory; file 02: 'exact SDK APIs and frameworks remain implementation design').
3. Define exit codes, D9 codes, fates, or their mappings from refusal families and joins (DR-007 HARD-BLOCKED chain; ID-DEP-2).
4. Provide a wire-level implementation, reference code, harness code, or fixtures - CC-1..CC-11 are class specifications with pass properties, not implementations.

5. Make performance, latency, or throughput claims of any kind; the two framing constants are hostile-input bounds, and every operational duration is deliberately unbound here (joinPrecedenceTable.deadlineDiscipline).
6. Define a canonical encoding, key ordering, escaping rule, or numeric normalization (controlFrameEncoding.encodingProfileDecision).
7. Define signing, trust, revocation, or the admission ceremony (DR-112/DR-G07); the handshake identity check is an agreement check only.
8. Map the transport to Windows: descriptor inheritance beyond 0/1/2 is specified for D-002's slice-1 platforms; Windows rides D-002's explicit platform deferral.

9. Claim a security sandbox: fd separation and supervision are fault-containment plumbing; file 02's rule stands - an unconstrained same-user component remains trusted code in the TCB unless effective confinement is enforced and measured (DR-G21 note).
10. Qualify anything for release, discharge any DR-111/DR-118/DR-G14/DR-G21 evidence cell, or move any register row: status is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and binds NOTHING.
11. Grant or define effect authorizations (F-5 is a courier; authorization is separate by the demarcation's own words).
12. Add lifetime rights: no pooling, no reuse, no keep-alive, no re-negotiation - the owning contracts' one-shot/no-reuse models and R-1 lifetime-neutrality stand untouched.

namedDifferencesFromPrototype.absenceStatement: Stated explicitly per prototype-evidence-reference.md ('A missing or inapplicable prototype baseline must be stated explicitly'): NO OUT-OF-PROCESS CONTROL PROTOCOL BASELINE EXISTS at pinned commit a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0. The prototype is in-process TypeScript; within the measured/searched bound recorded at recordedInputs.prototype.searchBound, it contains no length-prefixed stdio control framing, no control-channel version handshake, no identity binding on a channel, and no subprotocol negotiation. The transport, framing, handshake, negotiation, join-table, and conformance-class designs above therefore have NO prototype baseline; their analogues below are partial and named as such.

analoguesAndDifferences.prototype: External scanners run as one-shot batch execFile children: full stdout/stderr captured, parsed after exit (process-exec.ts, measured).
analoguesAndDifferences.contract: A live framed control channel beside an opaque data plane, with typed in-flight supervision. The prototype's typed spawn/kill/overflow fault distinctions (BINARY_MISSING vs SPAWN_FAILED vs KILLED_BY_SIGNAL; maxBuffer vs timeout) are the evidence kernel behind this contract's insistence on typed, distinguished channel events.

analoguesAndDifferences.prototype: Bundled-engine workers use Node fork() IPC JSON messages with no version exchange and an in-process fallback hatch for bundled engines (subprocess-transport.ts, measured; external tools always fork by trust tier).
analoguesAndDifferences.contract: One lifecycle/control model for every component, versioned and handshaked, with NO in-process fallback of any kind: DR-203 records the rejection of the prototype's split lifecycle/RPC models, and a fallback hatch is exactly the silent-substitution class D-008 forbids.

analoguesAndDifferences.prototype: Scanner output parsing is tolerant: JSON-lines with per-line error recovery and a tolerateNonJson skip of log preamble (json-lines.ts, measured).
analoguesAndDifferences.contract: Control frames are strict to the byte: duplicate members, unknown members, non-integer numerics, and oversize are typed refusals, never skipped. Tolerant ingestion of THIRD-PARTY batch output was load-bearing prototype pragmatism; a FIRST-PARTY control channel that tolerates malformed frames would convert every parser bug into silent protocol drift.

analoguesAndDifferences.prototype: Teardown is single-step SIGKILL on timeout (process-exec.ts), with separate, duplicated process-tree reaping machinery in the eval runner (process-tree.ts).
analoguesAndDifferences.contract: One deterministic five-step teardown ladder (J-5) with every transition and every bounded-wait expiry a typed event in one merged order - replacing the prototype's duplicate recovery machinery (rejected at DR-203) with a single host-owned model.

analoguesAndDifferences.prototype: signal-envelope.ts (measured) is the universal in-process result currency: schemaVersion 2, verdict header, units sidecar.
analoguesAndDifferences.contract: Deliberately NOT carried, parsed, or reinterpreted here: result/candidate envelopes are provider/data-plane and DR-125 territory. The control plane never carries a verdict - the nearest prototype shape to a 'result frame' is precisely what this contract walls off behind the opacity rule.

tensionsObserved.discipline: Reported, not resolved - per the authoring task. Each names the two texts in tension and what this candidate did pending resolution; none is settled by this artifact.

items.between: File 02's permitted function 'carry cancellation/health/resource/fault control' (control plane) VERSUS the applied TypeScript provider contract, whose closed host-to-worker frame set itself contains Cancel on stdin (delivery.v2, measured at digest; preserved by v4).
items.tension: Two cancellation carriers exist for the same child: the provider protocol's in-band Cancel semantic frame (owned by the applied V1 surface) and the control plane's cancellation function. File 02 assigns cancellation control to the control plane in its five-function list without stating how that composes with a provider protocol that already owns an in-band Cancel - injecting provider Cancel frames from the control plane would be the control plane authoring semantic frames (must-not list), while ignoring the in-band Cancel would starve the applied contract's own cancellation path.
items.pendingResolutionThisCandidate: Scoped control-plane cancel to SUPERVISION level (teardown-announcement) and left in-band Cancel wholly to the host's provider-side participant, with J-1 binding only the ordering. Whether that split is the intended reading of file 02 is for the coordinator/reviewer to decide.

items.between: File 02: 'negotiate an opaque named role subprotocol and version' (a live negotiation function) VERSUS file 04: 'project locks select exact signed index snapshot, component/artifact closure, platform alternative, subprotocol/state formats, and policy constraints' and 'each operation pins the project-selected generation for its entire lifetime'.
items.tension: If the lock/generation has already selected the subprotocol format and the operation is pinned for its lifetime, the handshake's 'negotiation' has no lawful freedom left - it can only confirm the pinned selection. Neither file states whether negotiation is a free runtime choice among manifest declarations or a confirmation of the lock's selection; the two readings produce different failure modes (a negotiation that 'succeeds' outside the pin would bypass generation pinning).
items.pendingResolutionThisCandidate: Offer-set construction intersects manifest declarations with the pinned generation where one exists (ID-DEP-6), which degenerates to confirm-only under a fully pinning lock - but whether locks MUST fully pin subprotocol tuples is DR-107/DR-111 design this artifact does not decide.

items.between: File 04's DR-111 matrix vocabulary - each surface's matrix declares 'migrations/bridges' - VERSUS file 02's demarcation and closing rule (no translation, no negotiation-made change).
items.tension: Applied to the control protocol's own row, a 'bridges' cell could be misread as authorizing the control plane to bridge between provider protocol versions - exactly what the closing rule forbids. The texts are reconcilable (bridges for CONTROL frames only) but nothing in file 04 says so.
items.pendingResolutionThisCandidate: compatibilityMatrixRow states the foreclosure explicitly for this row and leaves DR-111's vocabulary to DR-111.

items.between: The applied TypeScript provider binding 'stdout is protocol-only from process start through EOF' (delivery.v2) VERSUS this candidate's requirement that a provider-role child service the control handshake on fd3/fd4 before any data-plane byte flows.
items.tension: The applied contract is silent about descriptors beyond stdin/stdout/stderr and about any pre-protocol phase; it neither forbids nor provides for a control channel. Adding the control-channel obligation to provider-role components is an ADDITIVE build/packaging obligation that must enter through DR-103 manifest declarations and DR-120 adapter closure - it cannot be read INTO the applied provider contract, and this artifact does not do so. Sequencing composes only because the applied protocol's first frame is host-sent (Hello on stdin), so a child blocked on stdin awaiting it violates nothing while completing the fd3/fd4 handshake.
